newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power ends lower before Calif. nukes return.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power ends lower before Calif. nukes return.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Tuesday ahead of unit restarts at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) in southern California this week.
The West was the only region that suffered a downturn in power prices today, in sharp contrast with the rest of the country which saw spot electricity values catapult past the $100 a MWh level.

Southern California Edison today said the 1,070 megawatt (MW) SONGS unit 2 in San Clemente, Calif., was scheduled to reconnect to the grid tonight, a little later than previously expected after its repair outage.
The neighboring 1,080 MW SONGS unit 3 was set to resume operation by Thursday after being shut since April for refueling, maintenance and repairs.
In addition to the SONGS units, the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state continued to increase production. Its output reached 56 percent early Tuesday.
The 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming was expected to be restarted Wednesday.
August Palo Verde (PV) futures settled down 88 cents at $34.67 a megawatt hour (MWh), six cents above the day's low.
September PV finished down 75 cents at $21.83. Deferred PV contracts ended down 10 to 40 cents.
August California-Oregon Border (COB) settled down $1.00 at $21.53 a MWh, just three cents above the session low.
September COB finished down 82 cents at $21.83. Other COB months ended sic to 25 cents lower.
Steady cash prices and natural gas futures helped cushion the drop in power complex, brokers and traders said.
"Gas is up and daily prices are pretty strong," a Houston futures trader said.

Nevertheless, power futures will likely test the downside further as spot supply continues to increase, traders said, adding that the western market will keep tabs on the status of the SONGS units after they restart.
"They have to prove they could stay up," said a Midwest-based power marketer.
Day-ahead firm, peak power prices at PV firmed a dollar to $39.00-41.00 a MWh, while those at COB were little changed at $17.25-18.25.
NYMEX August Henry Hub natgas futures settled up 1.1 cent at $2.162 per million British thermal units after posting a high at $2.185.

While the interior section of the Southwest was forecast to stay hot into next week, the southern portion of the West Coast was expected to see dry, seasonal weather while the northern part would experience cool, overcast conditions.
Separately, southbound capacity of the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie transmission system will be cut by 250 MW to 3,200 MW between 0900 and 1600 PDT on Thursday and Friday for maintenance work.
